extracted.intended_audience: Workers, employers, small businesses, and other stakeholders who want to participate in OSHA rulemaking or submit public comments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for members of the public and stakeholder organizations on the OSHA rulemaking process and how to participate effectively (e.g., submitting comments, testifying, joining SBREFA consultations). Covers the seven-stage OSHA rule development process and best practices for comment content and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA initiates rule development through various triggers, including "new technologies or practices that better protect workers" and "injuries/illness affecting workers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These triggers indicate why OSHA may open a rulemaking effort; stakeholders should tie comments or data to these types of triggers when relevant (e.g., explain how a new technology improves protection or document workplace injuries that support regulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1: Pre-Rule (RFI/ANPRM)
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA gathers information through Requests for Information (RFI) or Advanced Notices of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM) to determine if regulation is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate early by responding to RFIs/ANPRMs; provide factual information, data, and real-world experiences to help OSHA decide whether to proceed to a proposed rule. Early engagement can shape the scope and framing of a future NPRM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stages 2-3: Proposed Rule (NPRM and SBREFA meetings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency publishes a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) explaining the proposed changes and conducts Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act (SBREFA) meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an NPRM is published, it will explain proposed regulatory text and rationale — use that text as the basis for detailed comments. SBREFA meetings are a formal avenue for small business input; small-business stakeholders should prepare to present specific compliance impact information at SBREFA consultations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stages 4-5: Final Rule Development (analysis of comments and rule drafting)
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA analyzes public comments and creates the final rule with implementation dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit thorough, evidence-based comments because OSHA will analyze the record and rely on comments to justify regulatory choices and implementation timelines. Provide data, cost/benefit information, and practicability considerations where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stages 6-7: Publication/Outreach (Federal Register and education)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule appears in the Federal Register alongside educational activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After publication expect outreach and educational materials; stakeholders should monitor Federal Register notices for final regulatory text and effective/implementation dates and plan compliance or further outreach accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation channels (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizens can engage through written comments submitted online via Regulations.gov, testimony at public hearings, participation in federal advisory committee meetings, and SBREFA consultations for small business concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the channel(s) that best fit your role and the substance you can provide: written comments for detailed documentary evidence; hearings for oral testimony and highlighting stakeholder perspectives; advisory committees for ongoing technical input; SBREFA for small-business-specific impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written comments via Regulations.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments submitted online via Regulations.gov are the primary mechanism for most stakeholders to provide input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA emphasizes: "Tell us how the issue impacts you, other workers, or your industry. Provide as much detail as possible." Include specific examples, data, citations, and suggested regulatory language when appropriate. Note procedural details like submission method and required docket identifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral testimony at public hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders may give testimony at public hearings convened as part of the rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hearings to amplify key points from written comments or to present personal/representative testimony. Contact OSHA with questions about hearing schedules and procedures in advance to ensure you are prepared to present within time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in federal advisory committee meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders can engage through federal advisory committee meetings to provide technical or policy advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory committees are appropriate for sustained, technical input; follow committee procedures for membership, comment submission, and meeting participation. Prepare detailed, evidence-based materials to share with committee members.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBREFA consultations for small business concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: SBREFA consultations are held to gather input from small businesses on potential regulatory impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses should use SBREFA meetings to present concrete information about compliance costs, operational impacts, and practicability. These consultations can influence regulatory flexibility and small-business considerations in the proposed or final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective comment content criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA guidance: "Tell us how the issue impacts you, other workers, or your industry. Provide as much detail as possible."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good comments explain real-world impacts, provide supporting evidence (data, studies, incident reports), suggest specific changes or alternatives, and, when applicable, include proposed regulatory text. Personal workplace experiences are acceptable and useful when describing effects on workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and procedural deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments close at "11:59 p.m. Eastern Time" on the stated closing date; stakeholders should plan submission ahead of that deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calendar the deadline (including timezone), allow time for uploading or docket issues on Regulations.gov, and contact OSHA with procedural questions before the close date. Late comments may not be considered in the rulemaking record.
